summary: Baileys fork contains char-code-obfuscated hardcoded endpoint in message-send path
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. In lib/Socket/messages-send.js at lines 425 and 436, the code assembles a URL via String.fromCharCode(...) that decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The destination is reconstructed from a decimal character-code array rather than appearing as a plain string, which conceals the host from casual inspection of the source. The obfuscated endpoint is embedded in the outgoing-message code path of a messaging library that handles user sessions, chat content, and credentials, so any consumer using this fork to send messages invokes a code path that reaches a non-Baileys, non-publisher third-party host controlled by the fork author. The char-code encoding of the destination is a deliberate concealment technique and is not consistent with legitimate configuration, telemetry, or vendor endpoints for this library family.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
